# Pascaal Console — full product brief

> AI components for safety and adoption.

## 0. Status and honesty

This console is a **UI preview**. It is a static site with mocked data. There is
no real authentication, no database, no API key registry, no signing key custody,
no revocation service, no usage meter and no payment processor. The sign-in form
accepts any email and password; nothing is transmitted or stored.

The target hosted console would live at `console.pascaal.com`. The design
rationale is in `docs/product-architecture.md` in the repository.

Canonical URLs:
- Company: https://pascaal.com/
- Protocol: https://hallmark.pascaal.com/
- Repository: https://github.com/Addyx2/hallmark
- Console architecture: https://github.com/Addyx2/hallmark/blob/main/docs/product-architecture.md

## 1. What Hallmark is solving

An agent acts on a provider's site. The provider needs to know who is
responsible, whether the agent is allowed to do this specific action, and how to
prove it later. Hallmark supplies a signed identity chain from a responsible
human to a short-lived, per-action grant, and a receipt for the decision.

The company builds AI components for safety and adoption. Adoption comes first:
observe cooperative agents, make attribution easy, give platforms useful traffic
intelligence. Safety comes second: at the responsible action, require an exact
grant and keep a receipt.

## 2. Identity model (target architecture)

Human identities:
- `User`: one human with a verified email; WebAuthn/OIDC preferred, magic link as
  bootstrap.
- `Session`: short-lived browser session, refresh token in an httpOnly cookie.
- `Organization`: permission and billing boundary.
- `Membership`: user × organization × role.
- `Role`: `owner`, `admin`, `developer`, `viewer`. In this UI preview the role
  matrix is shown in a banner and enforced client-side; the hosted product must
  enforce it server-side. Roles are scoped per organization.
- `Invitation`: email + role + expiry + single-use token.

Machine identities:
- `Project`: belongs to an organization, carries `tenant` (`hlm.tid`) and an
  audience (`aud`) used by gateways.
- `ApiKey`: belongs to a project, has a prefix, scopes, environment, created and
  last-used times, and a revocation state. Secret shown once; only a hash and
  prefix are stored. Example scopes: `freeroam:observe`, `barricade:enforce`,
  `grants:mint`, `registry:read`.
- Isolation: every read/write is scoped by `organization_id` first, then
  `project_id` / `tenant`. Unscoped requests fail closed.

Protocol identities:
- `Imprint`: signed root attestation binding a responsible human and an agent key
  (`cnf.jkt`), with a root budget.
- `Grant`: short-lived, single-action authority with `jti`, `sqn`, capability,
  budget and expiry.
- `RevocationManifest`: versioned denylist for keys, sessions, attestations and
  tenants. Freshness is enforced, not assumed.

## 3. Console screens in this preview

1. **Overview** — counters, quick links, current plan, boundary notice.
2. **Organizations** — switch org, create org (with a starter project), invite
   members, change roles, remove members. Owner/admin/developer/viewer roles,
   enforced in this preview and shown in a role-model banner.
3. **Projects & keys** — create projects with tenant + audience, issue scoped
   keys, reveal once (scoped to that org/project, cleared on navigation or sign
   out), revoke.
4. **Agents & grants** — agents by SPID and imprint, active grants, sequence
   numbers, budgets, revoke session, kill lineage.
5. **Traffic intelligence** — Freeroam observations: attributed vs unattributed,
   SPID, route, surface, method, anomaly flags, trend by day.
6. **Trackline** — PII-redacted receipts with pinned `HLM_` codes, mocked
   project/agent/time filters, and a redaction toggle that reveals `azp`, `ln`
   and `cnf` together. Receipt export is disabled in this preview.
7. **Usage & billing** — observed/enforced/minted/receipt volumes, four tier
   limits, illustrative invoices and overage. All mocked; costs are in mock cost
   units (100 units = $1).
8. **Docs for agents** — links to `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `/agent/` and a
   copyable setup prompt.
9. **Settings** — profile, security notes, reset preview state.

## 4. Freeroam framing (important)

Freeroam is the adoption wedge and is highly adaptable on the client side. A
platform can integrate it into any web surface and act as a vendor. The exact
user framing preserved here:

> "Freeroam seems to very adaptible on clients side as they can now decide to integrate it into any platform and be a vendor. They can easily see when agents use their website and analyse usage and traffic and even curb suspicous use."

Precise product meaning:
- Freeroam observes cooperative agent traffic and flags anomalies. It records
  attribution, route breadth, method mixes and new SPIDs.
- Freeroam **never denies** a request. It is not bot detection and makes no claim
  about classifying humans versus agents.
- To "curb suspicious use", the operator defines a **Barricade** surface at the
  first responsible action — checkout, write, license, destructive operation.
  Barricade checks the exact grant and emits a pinned `HLM_` denial when absent,
  replayed, expired, over budget, capability-mismatched or stale-revoked.
- Observation and enforcement are deliberately separate data paths. A visit is
  an observation; a grant is authority.

## 5. Trackline codes (examples used in this preview)

- `HLM_1003` bad_signature
- `HLM_1005` malformed
- `HLM_2004` replay_detected
- `HLM_6002` session_revoked
- `HLM_6003` attestation_revoked
- `HLM_6004` stale_revocation

Denials are pinned and safe to log. Default redaction masks each of `azp`, `ln`
and `cnf`; the toggle reveals all three fields explicitly. Grant expiry is shown
as a countdown (`in 29m`) and expired grants carry an expired badge. Revoking or
killing a grant preserves its last recorded budget total.

## 6. Service boundaries (target, not built)

Phase 3 adds `services/registry`, `services/mint`, `services/usage` and
`services/console-api`, plus managed revocation freshness with signed manifests.
The managed minting service never grants authority autonomously; it assists a
human ceremony. `docs/openapi.json` stays deferred until those services exist.

## 7. Security boundaries

- This preview stores no password and no real secret.
- Production must hash API keys, use short sessions, CSRF protection, rate
  limits, org-scoped authorization and audit logging.
- The console must never expose private signing keys.
- No remote key resolution: `jku`, `x5u`, `x5c` forbidden by spec.
- Grant surfaces fail closed on stale revocation. No silent fail-open.
- Do not call Hallmark ratified, certified or a standard until spec §21 closes.
  Use "Hallmark v1-draft conformant — spec commit <sha>".

## 8. Verification that is real today

- Spec: 21 sections, ~1,084 lines; 38/38 spec-wide vectors, 4/4 properties,
  4/4 enforcement points, crosscheck clean.
- Core SDK smoke: 6/6; CLI `self-test` and `verify`; tampered JWS yields
  `HLM_1003 / bad_signature / HTTP 401`.
- Provider wedge tests: 13 package tests + 1 end-to-end demo test.
- Local dashboard tests: mint → checkout verified, revoke → `HLM_6002`,
  kill-lineage → `HLM_6003`, frozen revocation + advanced clock → `HLM_6004`,
  reset. Counters are monotonic outside the audit ring buffer.
- Console preview tests: static surfaces and agent docs return 200.

## 9. Product status

- Hallmark: spec v1 open and executable, not ratified.
- Plots: in design.
- Waterguard: research.

## 10. How to integrate (conceptual)

1. Install `@pascaal/freeroam` on any web surface. It reads
   `Authorization: Hallmark <jws>` and `X-Hallmark-*` headers, verifies locally
   with pinned keys, emits safe events, and never blocks.
2. Read traffic intelligence to understand which agents use the site and where
   anomalies appear.
3. Define a signed Barricade policy for the first responsible action.
4. A human (leash) issues a short-lived grant for that exact action.
5. Barricade checks the grant, fails closed on problems, and writes a Trackline
   receipt.

The npm packages are staged locally and publish is pending the `@pascaal` scope
claim. Until then, use the repository workspaces.
